Problem 1: You are not specifying the timestamp format correctly. The function probably gave you the error message "Time format in data 23/11/2019 does not match with time format %d-%m-%y %H:%M:%S as specified by argument extEpochData_timeformat, please correct."

Problem 2: Similarly the epoch length you specified is not correct and GGIR probably gave you the error message: "The short epoch size as specified by the user as the first value of argument windowsizes (60 seconds) does NOT match the short epoch size we see in the data (15 seconds). Please correct."

I coded GGIR to give these error message such that GGIR users can read them and do not have to ask for help because the error message provides all the hints you need.

Best wishes,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Interpreting Vigorous Min vs ACC output
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Interpreting Vigorous Min vs ACC output
messages.body_plain:
Hi Reagan,

Assuming this question relates to part5 csv output:

dur_... variables such as dur_spt_wake_VIG_min and dur_day_total_VIG_min always have a value because even 0 minutes spent in a behaviour is informative.

ACC_... values are empty when no time was spent in a behavioural category, because average acceleration could not be calculated as there was no time spent in that behaviour.

I did this on purpose because filling in zero would be incorrect and skew the person level aggregates. For example, if a person typically moves with an acceleration of 300 during vigorous activity, but does not do vigorous activity on one day of the week, then the weekly average would indicate that they moved with 257 acceleration. That is inaccurate, and does not reflect the person's try typical acceleration in vigorous activity. On the other hand their typical time spent in vigorous activity should take into account the zero minutes spent on one of the days.

Maybe a metaphor helps: SpaceX shoots their rockets into space with a 4g acceleration but on many days of the year they do not shoot rockets into space, it would be meaningless to then say that the typical acceleration of SpaceX rocket launches is 0.1g only because all those days without a launch are allowed to be represented by 0 acceleration.

The advantage of this approach is further that by multiplying acceleration and duration you can get a volume measure of behaviour in that specific category. If we interpret acceleration as a proxy for energy expenditure per minute then this product would be a proxy for total calories burned. The unit of measurement would not be calories but the construct would be similar.

Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] P3 file NAFilename not recognized
messages.body_plain:
Hello Marcos,

As the error indicates: The file is empty or corrupt, which can happen.

To investigate:
Identify a specific file that triggers the error.
Read the file with GGIRread::readAxivity() function and check whether you can read at least some data from it.
If 2 is not successful, read the file with other tools such as OMGUI or https://github.com/OxWearables/actipy to read cwa data and check whether that allows for reading the file.
If 3 is successful and 2 is not then report this as an reproducible issue in https://github.com/wadpac/GGIRread. Otherwise it sounds like the file is truly corrupt or empty. Maybe the manufacturer can help you investigate further.

Thanks,

Vincent

Also, it it difficult to tell what guider was used and how it behaved from your screenshots. The guider column is missing in most of them. I see it is available in the first screenshot, but the guider for those nights state "nosleeplog", and I have never seen this definition of guider in GGIR. Did you modify this column?

When SPT is not identified, the last backup approach in GGIR is to define SPT from 21 to 7 (not 22 to 7), and this is very weird to occur, and in such a case, you would receive a warning. See here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/R/g.part4.R (lines 279:284).

It may be easier if you can identify one specific file for which this is occurring and if you are able to investigate what the data look like in those nights with the SPT defined from 22 to 7.

Best,
Jairo

messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent and colleagues,

We are running a project with ~700 participants (with another few hundred on the way) and are planning to investigate sleep questions alongside our physical activity metrics.

One of our first steps for QC on the sleep data is to use the "visualization_sleep" pdf output. It has been incredibly helpful for us in the past, but we are running into an issue with our current study.

Our IDs are structured like this: "Device_serial_number"_"Date_deployed" (e.g., 17-32323_2023- which is too long to fit on the side of the visualization sleep pdf (attached for reference). I have tried re-processing our data using idloc=2 to shorten the IDs, which worked for a subset of our data. However, with larger parts of our dataset, the serial numbers repeat, and GGIR can no longer correctly establish the start and end times for each participant. This gives us a lot more noise to comb through when QC'ing our data with the additional complication of connecting the shortened ID back to the actual participant (since the serial numbers repeat).

Is there a solution for specifying the dimensions or font size of the output for the visualization_sleep file so that our subject IDs are visible next to the sleep plots? We could potentially rig up a solution by creating temporary or different ID's, but I wanted to confirm that there was nothing simpler to be done on the GGIR/visualization side.

Thank you for your help, and please let me know if I can provide any other information!

Best,
Rob

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Questions GENEActiv Interpretation
messages.body_plain:
Re your question about the measurement period:

Your measurement period largely depends on what you're trying to capture. When you're trying to capture their free-living movement behaviour, 7 days including at least a weekend day is a good way to go. Then it's probably also desirable to increase your sampling frequency to e.g. 100 Hz. Here is just one example of using accelerometers in patient populations that show no relevant changes in movement behaviour beyond 7 days of measurement: https://bmcmedresmethodol.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12874-021-01350-6

Cheers

Fabian

messages.subject: Data extraction first day
messages.body_plain:
Dear all

I have an issue with extracting the data of the first day. Participants had to wear the Axivity for 3 months. Unfortunately, the battery only lasts around 14 days, so after these 14 days, they received a new Axivity (always around 10 in the morning, because we had movement sessions together and I wanted that specific PA-data).

If I run the script, the first day is not extracted and I don't know why specifically (start time = 10 am, wearing time = 10 am). Normally, if data_masking_strategy = 1, hrs.del.start = 0, hrs.del.end = 0, he should include all the data from start to end?

 Maybe someone is able to help me with this? Below you can find my script.

g.shell.GGIR( ### ==========================================================
      # General parameters #ADJUST PARTICIPANT NUMBER
      ### ==========================================================
      mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
      datadir =
      outputdir =
      studyname =
      overwrite = TRUE,
      do.report = c(2,4,5),
      nonwear_approach = "2023",
      ### ==========================================================
      # Part 1 parameters
      ### ==========================================================
      windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
      do.cal = TRUE,
      do.enmo = TRUE,
      do.anglez = TRUE,
      chunksize = 1,
      printsummary = TRUE,
      ### ==========================================================
      # Part 2 parameters #ADJUST MVPATRESHOLD
      ### ==========================================================
      data_masking_strategy = 1,
      hrs.del.start = 0,
      hrs.del.end = 0,
      ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
      mvpathreshold = c(104),
      ### =========================================================
      # Part 4 parameters #ADJUST TRESHOLD CUTPOINTS (Sanders 2019, GENEavtic/Axivity, non-dominant wrist)
      ### ==========================================================
      treshold.lig = c(57),
      treshold.mod = c(104),
      boutcriter = 0.8,
      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,
      boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
      boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
      boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,20,30),
      boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),
      boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),
      visualreport = TRUE,
      )

Thank you for your time!

Kind regards,
Evelien Iliano

messages.body_plain:
I have never worked with gt3x data so I don't know this, but maybe you need to use the extEpochData_timeformat argument.  The gt3x format, as far as I remember, does not carry timestamps you can read like this, so maybe it has nothing to do with it. From the manual:

extEpochData_timeformat
Character (default = “%d-%m-%Y %H:%M:%S”). To specify the time format used in the external epoch level data when argument dataFormat is set to “actiwatch_csv”, “actiwatch_awd”, “actigraph_csv” or “sensewear_xls”. For example “%Y-%m-%d %I:%M:%S %p” for “2023-07-11 01:24:01 PM” or “%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S” “2023-07-11 13:24:01”

Also, have you seen this?
If you are working with ActiGraph gt3x files, install the read.gt3x package with install.packages("read.gt3x")

messages.subject_clean: Questions in using NonWorn algorithm and calculating SRI
messages.body_plain:
Greetings!

First, I would like to express my gratitude to the developers and all contributors of GGIR, which benefited my works greatly.

I have a few questions regarding sleep detection in my current study design, which involves hip-worn actigraphy 24/7, except during sleep (the actigraph is removed before sleep and worn again after getting out of bed). NO sleep diary since we instructed participants not to wear while sleep.

In my case, the report seems to have correctly detected most of the non-wear periods (which correspond to the sleep periodsv in this design), but there seems to be an issue on day 5, and the wake-up time looks a little odd. Did I miss any arguments or settings to address such issues?

2. Since my study design does not include wearing the actigraph during sleep, I understand that calculating the Sleep Regularity Index might not be feasible based on the original protocol. However, it seems that GGIR might have a way of handling this missing data? I’ve read the relevant chapter in the BOOK and was wondering if I’m correct in this context. Could my manuscript still be valid for calculating SRI?

Here is my manuscript:
g.shell.GGIR(
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir="",
             outputdir="",
             #f0=f0, f1=f1,
             overwrite = TRUE,
             sensor.location="hip",
             do.imp=FALSE,
             idloc=2,
             print.filename=TRUE,
             storefolderstructure=FALSE,

             # Part 1 parameters:
             windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
             do.cal=TRUE,
             do.enmo = TRUE,
             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,
             printsummary=TRUE,

             # Part 2 parameters:
             strategy = 1,
             maxdur = 20,
             includedaycrit = 6,
             M5L5res = 10,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qwindow=c(0,8,21,24),

             mvpathreshold =c(69.1),
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             params_247=TRUE,
             epochvalues2csv=TRUE,

             # Part 3 parameters:
             do.part3.pdf=TRUE,
             anglethreshold=5,
             timethreshold= 5,
             ignorenonwear = FALSE,

             # Part 4 parameters:
             excludefirstlast = FALSE,
             includenightcrit = 6,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             HASIB.algo="ColeKripke1992",
             sleepwindowType="SPT",
             Sadeh_axis="Y",

             HASPT.ignore.invalid = NA,
             cosinor=TRUE,
             sleepefficiency.metric =2,
             IVIS.activity.metric = 2,
             IVIS_acc_threshold = log(20),
             IVIS_per_daypair = TRUE,

             # Part 5 parameters:
             excludefirstlast.part5=FALSE,
             save.ms5rawlevels=FALSE,
             threshold.lig = c(47.4),
             threshold.mod = c(69.1),
             threshold.vig = c(258.7),
             boutcriter = 0.8,
             boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,
             boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
             boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,20,30),
             boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),
             timewindow = c("WW"),

             # Report generation
             do.report=c(2,4,5),
             visualreport=TRUE, dofirstpage = TRUE, visualreport_without_invalid=TRUE,
             viewingwindow=2)

Thanks in advance!!!
Yue

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] ID issues in visualization_sleep.pdf
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rob,

At the moment GGIR offers no solution, we would have to change the GGIR code to show the ID in a different way.

However, in all studies I have worked with study participants have a unique ID that is separate from the device ID and because of that much shorter. For as far as I know Axivity, ActiGraph and GENEActiv all store the ID at the start of the filename separated by an underscore from the device serial number. So, I think you are better off updating the file names because in that way it will also be easier for your potential collaborators / future users of your data to process it with GGIR or any other software as it is unconventional to use such a long ID.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

On Thursday, 10 October 2024 at 9:32 AM, Rob Tennyson <robte...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear Vincent and colleagues,
>
> We are running a project with ~700 participants (with another few hundred on the way) and are planning to investigate sleep questions alongside our physical activity metrics.
>
> One of our first steps for QC on the sleep data is to use the "visualization_sleep" pdf output. It has been incredibly helpful for us in the past, but we are running into an issue with our current study.
>
> Our IDs are structured like this: "Device_serial_number"_"Date_deployed" (e.g., 17-32323_2023- which is too long to fit on the side of the visualization sleep pdf (attached for reference). I have tried re-processing our data using idloc=2 to shorten the IDs, which worked for a subset of our data. However, with larger parts of our dataset, the serial numbers repeat, and GGIR can no longer correctly establish the start and end times for each participant. This gives us a lot more noise to comb through when QC'ing our data with the additional complication of connecting the shortened ID back to the actual participant (since the serial numbers repeat).
>
> Is there a solution for specifying the dimensions or font size of the output for the visualization_sleep file so that our subject IDs are visible next to the sleep plots? messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Questions GENEActiv Interpretation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Fabian, recording exactly 7 days is commonly used but a very bad idea if you are interested in 24 hour behaviours or sleep. Recording for only 7 days means that we typically cannot record either the full daytime waking window or the full night on the first and last day of a recording. As a result, we typically end up with only 6 complete sleeponset-sleeponset or wakeup-wakeup-cycles. For example, UK Biobank made that mistake in their study protocol. The first day starts at 10am by which we cannot capture the full daytime waking window on that day and the last day ends at 10am by which we cannot be certain that the last sleep window is fully captured for all participants. As a result, the only realistic way to process that data is by processing it from the first sleep onset till the last sleep onset, which entails 6 windows.

Therefore, it is much more effective to aim for at least 8 days of accelerometer wear time and ideally 2 weeks or longer because that has been the standard in circadian rhythm research.

Cheers,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Data extraction first day
messages.body_plain:
Dear Evelien,

> the first day is not extracted

Which specific GGIR output are you referring to? In GGIR part2 csv reports we exclude the first day if it does not have enough valid hours, see parameter includedaycrit <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#includedaycrit>. Further, GGIR by default always starts at a round number of 15 minutes. For example, if your recording starts at 9:50 you will see results from 10:00 onward. We do this to standardise long epoch size (used as resolution for nonwear detection) and timing in a day.

Another reason why the start of a recording may look strange is if you did not specify the timezone and the data was collected in a different timezone.

Best,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Dear Kelsey,

Based on correspondence with other researchers I assumed that for sleep research it is critical to split diary guided analyses from non-diary guided analysis as we do in the GGIR part 4 output, while for compositional analysis any estimate of the night is acceptable because:
Sleep is only one of several components, by which a bit more uncertainty is considered acceptable.
If we only look at diary-guided sleep the drop in sample size might be too high given that we need complete data for two consecutive nights to describe a single day.

However, I understand that you may feel differently about this. I am happy to add an option to mask nights with no diary. However, that would then have to be done as paid consultancy. Please pm me if you are interested such that I can provide you with a quote.

Best,

Vincent

messages.subject: Heads-up problem in GGIR 3.1-3 and 3.1-4
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Hereby I would like to inform you about a problem with the recent GGIR 3.1-3 (only on GitHub August 14) and 3.1-4 (on both CRAN and GitHub).

In release 3.1-3 I added parameter 'nonwear_range_threshold' to allow user-control over the range threshold of the non-wear detection algorithm, and while doing this I also changed its default value to 50 mg because that seemed a great idea at the time.

However, we have now learnt that it was a bad idea as it prevents non-wear detection in some recordings. Therefore, in the upcoming 3.1-5 release I will reverse this to what it has been for the past 10 years (150 mg).

In the meantime if you were using GGIR 3.1-3  or 3.1-4 you can set nonwear_range_threshold to 150 to reverse the mistake.

Apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.

In an attempt to reduce the risk for similar mistakes in the future I have now assembled a GGIR user panel who I will inform about upcoming updates 2 weeks prior to each new release. If any update is not well motivated to them it will give us the opportunity to reconsider an update.

What could also help is if more people with an interest in R programming made an effort to dive into the GGIR code and tried to help improve it or its documentation. Only then an open-source project like GGIR can thrive.

Best regards,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] New to R and GGIR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mina,

To answer some of your questions briefly:

The aim is to investigate sleep in an older population, and also in association with physical activity. MVPA and steps are therefore also of interest. You can get all of these except steps for the hip from GGIR as generating steps from the wrist is currently done using an external function. ActiGraph has it's own step-counting algorithms for this which you may wish to look at. I am less familiar with the sleep side of things for anything other than the wrist. GGIR thresholds you have specified in your script look sensible for data from the wrist (e.g. anglethreshold = 5), but I would encourage you to seek out literature which has derived sleep metrics from the hip using GGIR, if there are any.
 The devices are set to record for a longer period of time than the participants actually wore it, but all were supposed to wear the device for 3 days (24h wear). This is fine because you can get the data for each day and night and trim to the dates that the participant wore the device, though alot of GGIR's prior steps for non-wear should also help to remove the days for you where the device was not worn. If you see that you seem to be missing days for participants that you would expect to be there, then the first thing might to increase `ndayswindow` to see if the participant just delayed wearing the monitor.

Does this code look right, or do anyone with experience have any input on other parameters I should include? And I guess it is best to process the wrist worn and hip worn separately? What is the best way to then process the hip worn? Yes it is best to process wrist and hip separately because you should also use different acceleration thresholds for light/mod/vig from the hip to the wrist - See some more info on site-specific cutpoints here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/CutPoints.html
You have a typo in your script: includedayxrit = 16 should be crit
If you are not using a test.csv for loglocation then remove this line

Another thing is that the devices have collected data at 100Hz. Can I still use GGIR? Yes 100Hz is absolutely fine and what probably most users have their data as.

Please use the extensive resources Vincent has developed to help inform on any other decisions - These can be found in the vignettes section here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/index.html

Thanks,
Ben
